findings.title: Internal contradiction: `k_first` "removed entirely" vs. "still parsed with deprecation warning"
findings.description: Technical Scope item 7 and the Technical Decisions §"k_first removed" commit to removing `k_first` entirely from the kernel, `ComputeConfig`, `Workload`, and `_NEIGHBOR_MODE_MAP`, with configs using it raising `ConfigurationError`. But Mitigation Strategies states: "Until then, ship the two new modes alongside the legacy `k_first` value (still parsed, with a deprecation warning) so the slice can land incrementally; flip the default and remove `k_first` parsing in the final commit." These are different shipped end-states (a mode that parses but has no kernel path is undefined behavior waiting to happen — if the config accepts `k_first` while the kernel no longer specializes for it, what does the tick do?). Pick one: either the mode is removed in the same commit as the kernel change (with `ConfigurationError`), or a documented transition state exists that specifies exactly what `k_first` does while deprecated. The current doc ships both statements.

findings.title: Exit criteria diverge from the parent slice plan entry without updating it
findings.description: The plan entry for slice 152 ([140-slices.simulation-scaling.md](project-documents/user/architecture/140-slices.simulation-scaling.md) item 13) defines the exit criteria as: "k-nearest TPS at N=200k **within 20% of k-first** TPS at the same N; parity preserved; **no regression on k-first path**." The slice design replaces the comparison baseline with `radius_only` (criterion 4) and removes `k_first` entirely — which makes the plan's "no regression on k-first path" unsatisfiable by construction. The engineering rationale for the redesign is well-argued, but the plan entry has not been updated to match, so the slice as designed cannot be checked off against its own plan definition. Update the plan entry (or keep `k_first` through this slice and remove it in a follow-up) so the plan's exit criteria and the slice's exit criteria agree.

findings.title: Dependency claimed shipped while its own documents show it unmet
findings.description: The slice states "Slice 150 is shipped on `main` as of 2026-05-05." Slice 150's design doc has `status: in_progress`, the slice plan shows item 11 unchecked (`[ ]`), and slice 150's own Implementation History records that its exit criterion 3 (TPS regression ≤ 20% vs. first-k-found at N=10k) is **not met** — "~88% regression" persists, with the coherent grid named as the fix. Slice 152's mechanism (reindex + mode-set change) in fact supersedes how 150's TPS criterion can be met, but the design should say so explicitly: state that slice 150 ships only in conjunction with 152, or that 152 relaxes/absorbs 150's TPS criterion. As written, the dependency claim conflicts with the recorded status of the dependency.

findings.title: Tier 3 NFR misstated: 200k vs. the architecture's 250k
findings.description: The slice repeatedly anchors on "the architecture's Tier 3 target (N=200k)" and "our current Tier 3 milestone of 200k." Both the architecture document (140-arch.simulation-scaling.md, §Envisioned State: "Tier 3 (250k...)") and the slice plan (§Scaling Tier Milestones: "Tier 3 (250k, ...)") define Tier 3 as **250k** on production-class hardware. The 200k gate itself is a reasonable dev-box checkpoint and matches the plan entry for slice 152, but attributing it to "the architecture's Tier 3 target" misstates the parent NFR. Restate it as what it is — a slice-level checkpoint below Tier 3 — or correct the N to 250k where the architecture is being cited.

findings.title: Measurement scope beyond the plan entry is cheap but could be deferred
findings.description: Criterion 3 requires a `radius_only` baseline at N=1M and verification step 5 requires new `mid-flock-500k`/`mid-flock-1M` workloads — none of which the plan entry assigns to this slice (its scope ends at the 200k gate + parity). These are bench-only runs, not code, so the cost is low and the FRNN follow-up trigger conditions genuinely need them; acceptable, but if the slice overruns, this is the first scope to defer to the FRNN follow-up slice's opening measurement.
